newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia replies to Bre-X/Barrick on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia replies to Bre-X/Barrick on Busang.

text.p: Indonesia said on Friday it had replied to a joint submission from Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp and urged the Canadian companies to settle with their local partners quickly.
"We have replied to the letter from Bre-X and Barrick today (Friday)," Umar Said, the mines and energy ministry secretary general, told Reuters.
"The letter says among other things that they must settle with their local partners soon," Umar said.

He did not give other details, but a source at the ministry said the letter also said the government "understood" an agreement between the two companies to split the richest parts of the Busang gold find 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government.

"We understand the agreement between Bre-X and Barrick on their wish to split 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government. It is contained in the letter," he said.
The source also said the Indonesian government was not likely to accept the involvement of Canada's Placer Dome Inc .
"I don't think the government will accept the involvement of Placer with Bre-X," the source, who is closely involved with the negotiations, said.

Placer chief executive officer John Willson said in Toronto on Tuesday that his company's offer of $5.0 billion to Bre-X for a merger was in the hands of President Suharto and top Indonesian ministers.
Bre-X estimates the Busang deposit contains at least 57 million ounces of gold, currently worth over $21 billion.
Complicating the issue is a C$2.0 billion (US$1.48 billion) lawsuit filed in Canada this week by Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims 40 percent of the Busang find.
Merukh has a 10 percent interest in the Busang I area of the gold find in East Kalimantan province. The richest ore however is in Busang II and III, where he is also claiming a stake.

Bre-X late last year announced a deal with a company headed by President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, under which it would receive $1.0 million a month for 40 months and a share of the Busang find when Bre-X received a contract of work.
Barrick is involved with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
Indonesian timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hassan, a close associate of Suharto, was also reported this week to have bought into a local company with a stake in Busang.

He did not give other details, but a source at the ministry said the letter also said the government "understood" an agreement between the two companies to split the richest parts of Busang 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government.

"We understand the agreement between Bre-X and Barrick on their wish to split 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government. It is contained in the letter," the source said.
The source also said the Indonesian government was not likely to accept the involvement of Placer Dome Inc.
